scores.evidence: CRDT: Yjs with y-prosemirror (conflict-free data type; no central server needed to order edits)
scores.rationale: Claims about CRDT/OT behavior, ack-after-commit durability, group commit, relative-position anchoring and Yjs compaction are accurate and precise, with only trivial imprecision ('state-vector hash').

scores.evidence: A web-based rich-text editor where many users edit the same document at once. Each user sees the others' edits and cursors live
scores.rationale: Covers all core capabilities (live co-editing, presence, history, sharing, tenancy), resolves ambiguities with stated assumptions, and explicitly defers non-essentials with trigger conditions in §10.

scores.evidence: Document affinity: all connections for one document land on one sync node via consistent hashing at the load balancer. Redis carries presence only
scores.rationale: Responsibilities, data ownership and consistency semantics ('saved' = durable commit) are defined once and honored consistently across phases, dependencies and validation with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: 0 divergent final states and 0 schema-invalid documents over ≥ 1M operations in ≥ 10k sessions, plus a 24 h soak
scores.rationale: V0–V6 tie checkable, labeled thresholds to the specific risks, validate the riskiest assumptions (convergence, durability) before commitment, define failure flips, and continue in production via divergence alerts and synthetic probes.

scores.evidence: each assumption is stated with what changes if it is false
scores.rationale: Every number is labeled ASSUMPTION or UNKNOWN with a stated basis, missing inputs list what flips if wrong, and no unsupported certainty appears.

scores.evidence: kill -9 of sync nodes, Postgres failover, partitions, disk-full; compare the client-side ledger of acknowledged updates with the persisted log
scores.rationale: Covers divergence, lost acks, duplicates (idempotent apply), malicious updates, telemetry leakage, revocation, hot documents, node loss and IdP outage, each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Rolling deploys drain WebSocket connections and clients reconnect... Rollback: Redeploy the previous image digest. Database migrations only add things
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback, add-only migrations, domain-meaningful signals (divergence metric, persist errors, SLO burn rate), runbooks, kill switch and on-call are designed in and sized to a stated team.

scores.evidence: Stored bytes ≤ 3× visible content after compaction
scores.rationale: Storage/infra cost drivers, scaling gates (V5 cost model, pricing gated on it) and controls are concrete, but build-side cost magnitude and engineering effort are not estimated, keeping it just short of 4.

scores.evidence: R3: the persisted update format and the client protocol sit inside every stored document and every open client
scores.rationale: Every decision carries an explicit reversibility class, revisit trigger and exit path, hard-to-reverse ones are validated earliest, and the point of no return is declared and guarded.

scores.evidence: Adopt open-source and self-host (Yjs, Hocuspocus, TipTap). Not a hosted provider
scores.rationale: Simplest workable topology (monolith + sync + worker, managed stores), proven libraries over custom work, speculative features explicitly deferred with trigger conditions, and no essential omitted.

scores.evidence: Staff user A signs in through OIDC, creates a document and types "hello". Staff user B, in a second browser, sees it live
scores.rationale: A dependency-justified build order with ordered tasks, checkable exit criteria per phase, concrete first slice, and explicit flips if validations fail means a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: CRDT: Yjs with y-prosemirror... → server-authoritative OT (operational transform: prosemirror-collab steps through a per-document central sequencer)
ProseMirror schema v1... server-side validation that rejects malformed or schema-breaking updates... `schema_version` on each document
fast-check property fuzz: 2–20 in-process clients making random edits... messages reordered, duplicated, dropped and re-sent; network partitions
Append-only update log plus periodic snapshots in Postgres... Ack-after-commit protocol... Snapshots and compaction in the worker
all connections for one document land on one sync node via consistent hashing at the load balancer... client reconnect with backoff
Short reconnect buffer: unacknowledged updates kept in IndexedDB and re-sent
Authorization on every WebSocket message (the server drops updates from viewers)... Revocation pushed to live sessions
Per-document version snapshots and restore... Version history UI and restore
Redis carries presence only... Presence cursors
Phase 5: Editor features and collaboration UX (the visible part, built last)
Heavy-edit documents (1 MB visible content, 1M-operation history): cold load time, sizes before and after compaction... 50 editors on one document
Schema-evolution protocol: version negotiation, forced reload, preserving unknown nodes (V6)... Mixed-version fuzz: clients on schema vN and vN+1

traps.evidence: Adopt open-source and self-host (Yjs, Hocuspocus, TipTap)
Phase 1: Document model and convergence... Phase 5: Editor features and collaboration UX (the visible part, built last)
"Saved" = acknowledged after a durable Postgres commit... Never ack before durable

note: An exemplary plan: proven CRDT stack validated before commitment, durability and authorization gated ahead of exposure, assumptions labeled with flips; only build-cost estimation is thin.
